note.note:
History:
- Main complaint: Poor appetite and low energy with low mood; episodic shortness of breath with palpitations, especially in elevators.
- Onset/duration/progression:
  - Appetite loss ~3–3.5 months (since changing to a new law firm).
  - Unintentional weight loss ≈ about a stone (~6 months).
  - Low mood and low energy for “months/long time.”
  - Palpitations/SOB occur prominently in lifts; not associated with walking initially reported, but later patient noted minimal recent walking, so exertional tolerance uncertain.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Intermittent nausea (no vomiting).
  - Headaches and nausea at work.
  - Sexual difficulties noted by spouse (“nightly activities”).
  - Denies chest pain and cough.
  - Bowels normal: no diarrhea, no blood, no mucus.
  - No reflux.
- Context: 35-year-old male lawyer; changed firms ~3.5 months ago; reports work/home generally “OK.” Decreased physical activity recently.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid).
- Medications:
  - Previously on levothyroxine (thyroxine); stopped taking since changing doctor months ago. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Other medications not documented.
- Allergies: Not recorded.
- Prior hospitalizations/surgeries: Not recorded.
- Family history/social habits: Not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Not recorded (telehealth visit; no vitals taken).
- Reported negatives: No chest pain; no cough; no vomiting; no diarrhea; no blood or mucus in stool.

Impression:
- Low mood with anorexia and unintentional weight loss; episodic palpitations/SOB in elevators; known hypothyroidism with cessation of levothyroxine. Etiology unclear; lab evaluation planned.
- Top plausible diagnoses (consistent with transcript):
  - Major depressive disorder or mixed anxiety/depression: Persistent low mood, low energy, reduced appetite, weight loss, sexual difficulties, functional impact.
  - Hypothyroidism relapse after stopping levothyroxine: Fatigue/low mood/inactivity; weight loss may reflect poor intake.
  - Situational anxiety/panic (claustrophobia) for elevator-triggered palpitations/SOB: Episodes specifically in lifts; no exertional dyspnea initially reported.

Management Plan:
- Tests:
  - Arrange “general set of bloods” as discussed: anemia screen (CBC), renal and liver function tests, vitamin levels.
  - Consider thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4) given history of hypothyroidism and medication cessation.
- Follow-up:
  - Review results and then arrange in-person physical examination if indicated.
  - Patient will receive a text to book a follow-up appointment after labs; was instructed to call support via app to schedule blood draw.
- Safety-netting:
  - Seek emergency care (A&E) for chest pain or significant/worsening palpitations.
  - Contact clinic promptly if bowel habits change or vomiting develops.
  - If feeling poorly, do not wait for automated messages; call the service.

Patient Summary:
- A 35-year-old male reports several months of low mood, low energy, reduced appetite, ~1 stone weight loss over ~6 months, and elevator-triggered palpitations/SOB. He has hypothyroidism and stopped levothyroxine months ago. Labs have been ordered to evaluate constitutional symptoms and guide next steps.

Key Takeaways:
- Get the ordered blood tests done promptly by calling the support number in the app.
- Go to A&E for chest pain or severe/worsening palpitations; contact the clinic for new vomiting or changes in bowel habits.
- Expect a text to book follow-up once results are available; call sooner if feeling worse.

Next Steps:
- Complete blood tests (CBC, renal/liver profile, vitamin levels; consider thyroid function tests).
- Schedule follow-up to review results and determine need for in-person exam and targeted treatment.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies; complete medication list and doses; vitals; physical exam; quantified weight change; sleep history; substance use (alcohol/caffeine/illicit); family history; mental health screening (PHQ-9/GAD-7); suicide risk assessment; detailed sexual history; red-flag review (fevers/night sweats); TB/travel exposures.
- Conflicts/ambiguities: Exertional tolerance unclear—initially reports no dyspnea with walking a mile, later notes minimal recent walking; trigger context for palpitations (closed spaces vs specifically lifts) somewhat ambiguous due to audio gaps.
- Transcript quality: Several inaudible/truncated segments and unclear phrases (e.g., exact weight amount, some sentences cut off), limiting precision.
